findings.reason: One essential bar versus an empty diagram returns zero because both finite projections are empty. Equal finite endpoints in different dimensions also cost zero.
findings.limits: The code documents finite-point matching and shell status, so this is a scope and silent-projection gap in the general diagram API, not a defect of ungraded finite matching itself.

findings.reason: Exact rational costs are converted to f64 and powered with no returned error bound or underflow/overflow refusal. A positive rational 1/2^1100 is below binary64 range and its diagonal distance can collapse to zero.

findings.reason: At q=1/2, A={(0,100),(10,110)}, B={(1,101),(10,110)}, C={(1,101),(11,111)} yield distances 1,1,4, violating the triangle inequality.
findings.limits: The implemented positive-q objective is well defined as a cost; restricting the metric claim to q>=1 resolves this specific issue.

findings.reason: Memo size is checked before recursion and updated afterward, leaving active recursion states uncharged. A three-element total order with max_downsets=1 returns one extension while visiting and storing three nonempty downsets.

findings.reason: Plain Deserialize derives accept private fields without routing through nonempty/order/orientation/closure/index validation. An empty vertex vector can reach len-1; inconsistent cached indices or arbitrary orientation can invalidate later operations.

findings.limits: Only the exact count was computed; no large object allocated. The public budget explicitly names maximal chains, so this is a resource-bound limitation across that call rather than a false count of maximal chains.

findings.limits: A grammar composed exclusively from unchanged nested constructors avoids this example. This is not a failure of the downstream matrix shape/product check.
